subject: gk
question: In which of the following years was there an all-India campaign in opposition to the all-white Simon Commission?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Simon Commission** was a group of seven British Members of Parliament that came to India in **1928** to study constitutional reform.
 
• The commission was called the **Simon Commission** after its chairman, **Sir John Simon**.
 
• It was an **all-white commission**, meaning it had no Indian members, which led to widespread protests and opposition throughout India.
 
• The Indian National Congress and other political parties boycotted the commission, demanding **self-rule** and **inclusion of Indians** in the discussion for constitutional reforms.
 
• Prominent leaders like **Lala Lajpat Rai** strongly opposed the commission, and during one of the protests, he was brutally lathi-charged by the police, which eventually led to his death.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1939**__

 __
 
• **1939** was significant for the start of **World War II** and the subsequent Indian involvement in the war.
 
 
 
• **1922**__
 __
 
• The year **1922** is known for the **Chauri Chaura incident**, which led to Mahatma Gandhi calling off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 
 
 
• **1942**__
 
 
• **1942** is notable for the launch of the **Quit India Movement** by Mahatma Gandhi, demanding an end to British Rule in India.
